title: Ang 15–20: Nanak in Sri Rag
hookLine: greed, falsehood and the Name, in Guru Nanak's hymns
tomorrow: what does a fish know about the river it lives in?
last: THE FIRST RAGA: LET ME NOT FORGET.

cards: A pinch of salt, a squeeze of lime, one more chili: some cooks taste a pot again and again before it's right, and can tell you exactly what it's missing. Flavor is a language. Sweet, salty, sour, hot.
On ang sixteen, Guru Nanak speaks that language, and gives each taste a meaning.

teach.b: The hymn is built like a meal. In paraphrase: all tastes are sweet in believing, and salty in listening. Tart and sour in speaking the Word aloud; the spices are the music.
And the thirty-six flavors of nectar are love of the One, for the one on whom the gracious glance falls.

Then the refrain, in paraphrase: O Baba, the pleasure of other food is ruin; eating it, the body is hurt and wrongdoing enters the mind. Notice two old friends from the Japji: mannai, believing, and suniai, listening.

teach.h: LOVE OF THE ONE: THE WHOLE FEAST.
teach.b: Something to tell someone tonight: in Sri Rag, Guru Nanak builds a whole meal out of listening, believing, speaking, music and love.
The pages around it, angs fifteen to twenty, keep coming back to the same table: greed that can't stop eating, falsehood that tastes fine and leaves you hungry, and the Name as the food that fills.

teach.h: THE OTHER FOOD HURTS BODY AND MIND.
teach.b: The other food in the refrain isn't dinner.
It's whatever we keep reaching for that hurts body and mind.
So Nanak's Sri Rag asks a cook's question: what are you actually tasting?

how: Guru Nanak's hymns in Sri Rag fill the pages from ang 14 on; Sikhs read and sing them in the gurdwara and at home, and in a sehaj path they come right after the daily prayers.

games.q: the meal on ang 16 — tap the pairs.

s: in this Sri Rag hymn, Guru Nanak calls listening salty
all tastes are sweet in believing, salty in listening.
the hymn tells Sikhs to give up tasty food
it warns against the other food that hurts body and mind, and names a better taste: love of the One.
the thirty-six flavors are a list of real dishes
they're the flavors of nectar: love of the One, for the one the gracious glance falls on.

games.q: a friend fills every quiet minute with snacks and scrolling and says she still feels empty. what would the ang 16 hymn point toward?
o: a stricter diet: the hymn is about cutting out tasty food.
a different taste: listening, believing, love, the food the hymn praises.
more variety: thirty-six flavors means try a bit of everything.
games.why: the other food in the refrain is whatever hurts body and mind; the hymn's full feast is love of the One, with listening and believing as its flavors.

practice: If something is close by to taste, a sip of water, a bit of fruit, a grain of salt, taste it slowly and let the flavor fill your mouth before you swallow.
If nothing is near, breathe in through your nose and notice whatever the air carries. Stay with that one taste or scent, and let it be enough.

wordCard.voice: Ang 15. Where Guru Nanak's own hymns fill Sri Rag, on greed, falsehood and the Name. Today's word.
